speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Um, and we are using that as signals on the PR for the agent to go fix.
zh: Um，我们将其用作 PR 上的信号，供智能体去修复。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: So Code Rabbit and the and uh our internal Zool posts comments back on the PR, uh, and we have failures in CI when some tests don't pass, or um some we do some uh what's it called, mutation testing, uh property-based testing, a whole bunch of that kind of stuff.
zh: 所以 Code Rabbit 和 uh 我们的内部 Zool 在 PR 上发回评论，uh，当一些测试不通过时，我们在 CI 中有失败，或者 um 我们做一些 uh 它叫什么，变异测试，uh 基于属性的测试，一大堆这类东西。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: If those don't pass, those all get posted back as signals on the PR.
zh: 如果那些没有通过，所有这些都会作为信号发回到 PR 上。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: The orchestrator is watching the PR, and so we'll re-wake the agent when those comments are uh passed back, and the agent then goes fixes them.
zh: 编排器正在关注这个 PR，所以当这些评论被传回时，我们会重新唤醒智能体，然后智能体去修复它们。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Uh it will take in the comments, it will reason over them, uh, it then responds in line in those comments where appropriate or as a top-level comment, resolving where appropriate um as needed, and also potentially escalating back to human uh for review.
zh: 它会接收这些评论，会对它们进行推理，然后适当地在这些评论中内联回复，或者作为顶级评论，在适当的地方解决它，或者可能还会升级回人类进行审查。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: So it has the ability to say, hey, I need context, can pause everything and go post that question back on the linear ticket, which then notifies the human.
zh: 所以它有能力说，嘿，我需要上下文，可以暂停一切，然后把那个问题发回到 linear ticket 上，这会通知到人类。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Um, and so that is kind of the flow in a nutshell.
zh: 所以这就是流程的概况。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Uh going from a linear ticket to orchestrator to coding agent unboxed to PR to a bunch of cycles on the PR review between automated bots and uh CI checks uh back to the agent until it gets to a state that is good.
zh: 从一个 linear ticket 到编排器再到开箱即用的编码智能体，再到 PR，然后在自动机器人和 CI 检查之间的 PR 审查上循环往复，再回到智能体，直到达到一个良好的状态。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: That's normally when we flip to uh in review and we'll get the human in order to engage with that, uh, because it's kind of like in hopefully the best state that it could possibly be.
zh: 那通常就是当我们转换为“正在审查”的时候，我们会让人类参与进来，因为那希望是它可能达到的最佳状态。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: And so human, the interaction mode there is twofold.
zh: 所以人类，那里的交互模式是双重的。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: One, uh we do have the escape hatch of they can uh pull down the branch locally, make changes themselves, and then push it back up.
zh: 第一，我们确实有一个逃生舱门，他们可以在本地拉下分支，自己进行更改，然后再推回去。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: That's always an option if kind of it's gonna be quicker or they need to do it that way.
zh: 如果那样更快或者他们需要那样做，这总是一个选项。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: What we're trying to push for though is doing the interaction mode on that PR surface via comments, uh, because that then allows us to kind of track that and also integrate that back into kind of what a review philosophy is.
zh: 但我们试图推动的是，通过评论在 PR 表面上进行交互模式，因为这让我们能够跟踪它，并将其整合回我们的审查理念中。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: That makes it surfaceable, actionable, so that we can kind of continue to leverage agents uh or continue to leverage those insights into better review flows so that we don't need to get a human to identify that stuff again in the right.
zh: 这使其变得可见、可执行，这样我们就可以继续利用智能体，或者继续利用这些洞察来改进审查流程，这样我们就不需要让人类再在右侧去识别这些东西。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: And that's just for those pull requests that do require a human interaction for for a review.
zh: 这仅适用于那些确实需要人类交互来进行审查的拉取请求。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: Exactly.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: Awesome.
zh: 太棒了。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: So the orchestrator in this sense actually does sound like kind of what a human would do today in in that kind of flow.
zh: 所以从这个意义上说，编排器听起来确实很像人类今天在那个流程中会做的事情。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: So it's uh And and and let's talk a little bit about each step there because you know if if we were to um you know ask an agent to do various things, whether it's coding, whether it's design, whether it's a bit of architecture work or whatever, at the various stages, it's not always going to get it right.
zh: 所以它是呃，我们稍微谈谈那里的每一个步骤，因为你知道，如果我们呃让智能体做各种事情，不管是编码、设计，还是一些架构工作或其他什么，在各个阶段，它不总是能做对。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Um so twofold.
zh: 双重的。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: One is we intentionally shift task ownership and task decomposition onto the human at the moment.
zh: 一是我们有意地将任务所有权和任务分解转移给了人类。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: So we're not saying give the dark factory your Q1 plans and it will go do all of that for you.
zh: 所以我们不是说把你的 Q1 计划给暗工厂，它就会去为你做所有这些。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: We're saying give the dark factory a well-scoped linear ticket like you would to a junior or mid-level engineer, um, and it will go implement that for you.
zh: 我们是说给暗工厂一个范围明确的 linear ticket，就像你给初级或中级工程师那样，它会去为你实现它。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: And so there is an expectation that there has been a fair amount of design work, design thinking, potentially whiteboarding, potentially uh discussion beforehand, um, which you are then able to encode in the linear ticket, which then kind of guides the agenti implementation after that.
zh: 所以期望是有相当数量的设计工作、设计思维、可能是白板画、可能是之前的讨论，然后你能够将这些编码在 linear ticket 中，这会在随后指导智能体的实现。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: And so think of it as your job no longer is take ticket and go implement it.
zh: 所以把它想象成你的工作不再是接取工单并去实现它。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Your job is have the whiteboarding conversation with your colleagues, capture that either as like a granola transcript or a screenshot or whatever, and then work with an agent to then translate that into a set of tickets that the Dark Factory can then go implement for you.
zh: 你的工作是和你的同事进行白板对话，将其捕获为 granola transcript 或截图或其他任何东西，然后与智能体合作，将其转化为暗工厂可以为你实现的一组工单。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Um, so there's a little bit of that shift of prior work up front.
zh: 所以有一点前期工作的转移。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: In terms of the actual does it follow what you do?
zh: 关于它是否遵循你所做的？

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: There's uh one thing is implementation is now free or functionally free.
zh: 有一点是，实现现在是免费的，或者功能上是免费的。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: You have to pay token costs.
zh: 你必须支付 token 成本。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: So kick off six, kick off seven.
zh: 所以启动六个，启动七个。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Like you've got a couple ideas, just go kick them off and don't send them an auto merge and go look at the code.
zh: 就像你有几个想法，直接去启动它们，不要自动合并它们，去看看代码。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Like I kind of almost view the fact that there is a potential like wide state space of potential solutions as either you don't care about it, and so you should accept whatever satisfies it, or B, you're unsure, and so you should use the agents to then help explore that state space and you can ground your analysis in a real code artifact, like how it looks and how it feels, rather than just in the theoretical abstract of I think this is gonna feel nicer if the interface is designed this way or that way.
zh: 我有点几乎把这样一个事实视为，潜在的解决方案的广阔状态空间，要么是你不在乎它，所以你应该接受任何满足它的方案，要么 B，你不确定，所以你应该使用智能体来帮助你探索那个状态空间，你可以将你的分析建立在一个真实的代码工件基础上，比如它的外观和感觉，而不是在理论抽象中，我认为如果界面这样设计或那样设计感觉会更好。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: And so that kind of approach I think is quite powerful because it does it's allowing you to kind of do more experimentation because you do then don't need to run the experiments, Darfactory does it for you, and you're just kind of looking at the outputs of that.
zh: 所以我认为这种方法非常强大，因为它确实允许你做更多的实验，因为你不需要运行实验，暗工厂会为你做，你只是看着它的输出。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Um, on the taste and the architecture specifically, our solution to that has been verifiers, which are basically kind of like natural language single statements that can resolve to yes or no to a Boolean about a specific piece of code.
zh: 关于品味和架构，我们的解决方案是验证器，它们基本上是自然语言的单句陈述，可以解析为是或否，对应于特定代码片段的布尔值。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: And so they're the mechanism that we're giving engineers to kind of instill principles about the code um into their own specific parts of the code base that will then only trigger when those parts of the code base are modified.
zh: 所以它们是我们给工程师的机制，将代码原则灌输到他们自己的代码库特定部分，这些部分只会在这些代码库部分被修改时触发。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Um and so that's a deterministic trigger, or that's it's a deterministic trigger, but it is sent to an LLM as a judge in order for the Boolean evaluation.
zh: 所以那是一个确定性触发器，或者那是一个确定性触发器，但它被发送给 LLM 作为法官来进行布尔评估。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Um so think along the lines of something like these files should uh only ever import from other library files.
zh: 所以想一下这样的事情，比如这些文件应该只从其他库文件导入。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Yes, you can technically write a very convoluted regex um in order to do that as a deterministic lint rule, or you can encode that principle of like, hey, we want library to be the single source of truth, and so things should only ever be importing from the library and should never be importing from other modules within the code base in order to uh kind of maintain dependency, clean dependencies.
zh: 是的，你可以在技术上写一个非常复杂的正则表达式，把它作为一个确定性的 lint 规则，或者你可以编码这个原则，嘿，我们要 library 作为唯一的真实来源，所以东西应该只从 library 导入，绝不应该从代码库内的其他模块导入，以为了保持依赖，干净的依赖。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: And so that kind of taste is really hard to write deterministic rules for, and we've historically kind of caught it in code review.
zh: 所以这种品味真的很难写出确定性规则，我们在历史上是在代码审查中捕捉到它的。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Agentic code review is uh is expensive and slow.
zh: 智能体代码审查既昂贵又缓慢。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Can we shift kind of these discrete chunks into a human legible form that we can then put next to the code so that the agents can go bang their head against the wall in terms of making them pass um as part of the CI flow?
zh: 我们能把这些离散的块转移成人类可读的形式，然后放在代码旁边，这样智能体就可以在 CI 流程中把它们撞到墙上去让它们通过吗？

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: So I think that's a little bit of the shift in framing as well.
zh: 所以我认为框架也有点转变。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: And it does feel like those like I think you've alluded to that, the verifiers are very, very fast to run.
zh: 这确实感觉像你暗示的那样，验证器运行得非常非常快。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: In terms of the this, you know, the the the task that the agent is trying to do as part of that verifier, um it sounds like the scope is much, much smaller as well.
zh: 关于智能体试图作为验证器一部分做的任务，听起来范围也小得多。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: So for example, if that, you know, if that one check was part of a code review, it feels like that's gonna be missed by an LLM because not all the time, but that's gonna be missed by an LLM some of the time because the code review covers a huge number of things.
zh: 所以举个例子，如果那个检查是代码审查的一部分，感觉 LLM 会漏掉它，虽然不总是，但 LLM 有时会漏掉它，因为代码审查涵盖了非常多的事情。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: Whereas if it's a small scoped uh piece that an LLM just needs to check on this file or on this set of files, this one thing, it's gonna have a higher chance of actually actually validating whether that's done or not.
zh: 而如果它是一个小范围的片段，LLM 只需要检查这个文件或这组文件这一件事，它实际上验证是否完成的机会就会更高。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Correct, yeah.
zh: 正确，是的。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: And so like a bit of our philosophy is a genetic code review should be the catch-all for things that we miss.
zh: 所以我们的一些理念是，通用代码审查应该是我们遗漏事物的兜底。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: But once we have identified something that we think is important, we should be shifting them to verifiers if we can, because as you mentioned, they're a lot cheaper to run.
zh: 但是一旦我们确定了我们认为重要的东西，如果可以的话，我们应该将它们转移到验证器，因为正如你提到的，它们运行起来更便宜。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: It's an LLM call over the diff.
zh: 这是一个针对差异的 LLM 调用。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Um, and so we can uh assess that.
zh: 所以我们可以评估那个。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: And we also run one LLM call per verifier.
zh: 而且我们也对每个验证器运行一次 LLM 调用。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: So that LLM is really just reasoning about this single verification, not about all of the conflicting priorities that it might have in its head.
zh: 所以那个 LLM 实际上只是在推理这一次验证，而不是关于它脑海中可能拥有的所有相互冲突的优先级。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: So we're trying to kind of sketch out a boundary around the code, around like what is acceptable code from a bunch of different points rather than trying to build like a smooth, a smooth line, basically, in a skill or in an injector review or something along those lines.
zh: 所以我们试图在代码周围勾勒出一个边界，围绕一堆不同观点中什么是可接受的代码，而不是试图建立一条平滑的，一条平滑的线，基本上，在技能或者注入器评审或类似的事情上。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: The other kind of principle that we have is anything that is a verifier that we can make deterministic, fully deterministic, well then we should make that deterministic.
zh: 我们拥有的另一个原则是，任何我们可以做成确定性的验证器，完全确定性，那么我们就应该让它变成确定性。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: I think historically a lot of people haven't written really complex link rules because they're annoying and finicky and they slow human engineers down and they're hard to write.
zh: 我认为历史上很多人没有真正编写复杂的链接规则，因为它们很烦人而且挑剔，并且拖慢人类工程师的速度，而且很难写。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Well, right now we have no human engineers.
zh: 嗯，现在我们没有人工程师。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Agents are fine with annoying Infiniki, they can very happy to go bang their heads against the wall in order to make something work.
zh: 智能体对烦人的 Infiniki 没问题，它们可以很高兴地去撞墙以让事情运转起来。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Uh and they're not quick, but like an agent can write it.
zh: 呃，而且它们不快，但是像智能体可以写它。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Doesn't matter to me how convoluted it is.
zh: 它是多么曲折对我并不重要。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: And so that then allows us to not even pay the LLM costs, then we're just playing the CPU cost of kind of uh deterministic uh verification in that regard.
zh: 因此这让我们甚至不需要支付 LLM 成本，那么我们只是支付 CPU 成本，关于那种呃确定性的呃验证在那个方面。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: And so it's like a sequencing almost for engineers to kind of build their the things that they had in their head around quality or around what good code looked like or how good code smelt.
zh: 所以这几乎就像是一个排序，为了让工程师围绕质量或者围绕好代码的样子或者好代码闻起来是什么样的去建立他们脑海中的东西。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: We can kind of put that into the code base in that sequence of the very, very quick deterministic verifiers, linting rules, the uh LLM as a judge verifiers that are just over the diff, which are natural language and so probably too fuzzy to express, but easy enough for a good reasoning model to understand, and then the catch-all agentic review.
zh: 我们大概可以把那个放进代码库，在那个非常、非常快的确定性验证器、链接规则、LLM 作为评判的验证器的序列中，这些只针对 diff，是自然语言的所以可能太模糊而无法表达，但对于一个好的推理模型来说足够容易理解，然后是全能的智能体评审。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: One of the really interesting things about, I think, about that sequence is that we can run automatic promotion.
zh: 关于那个序列，我认为，真正有趣的事情之一是我们可以运行自动晋升。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: So every night we look at kind of the PR comments that are being posted by agentic review and human review, and we assess whether any of those should be verifiers.
zh: 所以每天晚上我们查看由智能体评审和人类评审发布的 PR 评论，我们评估其中是否有任何应该成为验证器。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: And so we can kind of continually shift left in that regard to get faster, to get quicker, to get cheaper, but also importantly as well for me, I think, to get more human legible.
zh: 所以我们可以大概在那个方面不断地左移，以变得更快，变得更迅速，变得更便宜，但对我而言，重要的是也为了变得更人类可读。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: If I look at a verifier, it's much easier for me to reason about that than to read a long skill.md and figure out uh is this thing going to be correctly weighted for something that I think is really important against all of the other compounding trade-offs that it might have.
zh: 如果我看一个验证器，对我来说推理那个比读一个长的 skill.md 并弄清楚呃这个东西是否会被正确地权衡，针对我认为很重要的东西，相对于它可能拥有的所有其他复合权衡，要容易得多。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: Super interesting.
zh: 超级有趣。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: Let's go into what worked and what didn't work.
zh: 让我们深入探讨什么有效，什么无效。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: Obviously, this unlocked, it sounds like a ton.
zh: 显然，这解锁了，听起来像是很多。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: Yep.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: Um what were the biggest learnings you had early on with this?
zh: 呃关于这个你早期最大的学习收获是什么？

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Uh coding agents are really good, and if you give them a wide enough scope, they will do some great things.
zh: 呃编码智能体真的很棒，如果你给它们足够宽的范围，它们会做一些很棒的事情。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: I think there was definitely a bit of a kind of bias internally going from kind of going from a philosophy of I've got to be their babysitting the coding agent to I shoot, I'm I can't even look at the logs for this because it's running on a sandbox in the cloud.
zh: 我认为内部肯定有一种偏见，从一种我必须做编码智能体的保姆的哲学转变到我天哪，我甚至不能看日志因为它运行在云端的沙箱中。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Um, I better make sure that my tickets are super well scoped and super small and super tiny, kind of like intern-level tickets.
zh: 呃，我最好确保我的票据范围非常非常好、非常小、非常小，就像实习生级别的票据。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: And now we've slowly been, and this is cultural, not technical, slowly been relaxing those constraints.
zh: 现在我们慢慢地在，这是文化的，不是技术的，慢慢地在放松那些约束。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: And people have been like, ah, cool.
zh: 人们一直说，啊，很酷。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: What is actually the biggest thing that I can give to the dark factory and see it produce something that is relatively valid as a result?

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: And so the tickets, was that a trust issue?
zh: 所以那些票据，那是信任问题吗？

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: It was trust it was pure trust issue.
zh: 是信任，那是纯粹的信任问题。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: I think trust comfortability seeing seeing the results.
zh: 我认为信任舒适度，看到看到结果。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: We're asking people to trust that something that is kind of hidden, it's called a dark factory because we're not looking at the logs as it's kind of operating.
zh: 我们要求人们信任某种隐藏的东西，它被称为黑暗工厂因为在它运作的时候我们不看日志。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: We are postdoc, but not kind of in the actual operations.

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Um, they need to be able to trust that that's going to do something that they would be okay with.
zh: 呃，他们需要能够信任那会做一些他们会认可的事情。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Because ultimately, like we still have an accountability mechanism.
zh: 因为最终，像我们仍然有一个问责机制。

speaker: Rob Willoughby

en: What what problems did you have then?

en: So just uh on that trust bit, I think one of the things that we've been trying to do on the team to build that trust is by uh running as far ahead as we can and running into the walls early and uh mucking up, basically.

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: So we definitely have that.

en: Let's go deep there.

en: So I think um the most interesting there's two kind of classes of ones, one around context and one around um verification.

en: In terms of context, uh I pull data for the number of slack threads uh sent on our team channel uh versus the other team channels kind of every week.

en: We have had to overcommunicate everything that we're doing because we are doing so much more quicker.

en: And I'm not, I don't think people actually go look at code anymore because they're all just using agents.

en: So we need to build the signals and the context on top of that to give us trust that this is working the way that we think it's gonna be working, but then also we know what everyone else is gonna be doing.

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: And that and that 95% that is of the dark factory.

en: Yes, of the dark factories, basically.

en: Yes, everyone has looked at the project code base.

en: Again, we have human review required there, so that has been looked at, but it's for the dark factory itself.
zh: 再次强调，我们在那里需要人工审查，所以那部分已经被看过了，但这是针对 dark factory 本身的。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Um, and so we needed to figure out mechanisms in order to make sure that everyone knew what they were doing, make sure that everyone was comfortable with their own work getting thrown away, and make sure that we understood how the code base was changing over time.

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Um, and so we definitely still haven't figured this out.
zh: 呃，所以我们肯定还没弄明白这个。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: I still will wake up on some days and be like, uh, I didn't, I don't think that's a good idea.

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Why did that land?
zh: 为什么那个合并了？

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Yeah.

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: But the intention, what we're trying to do there is overshare the context so that we're aware, but then also fix forward.
zh: 但其意图，我们要在那里做的就是过度分享上下文以便我们知晓，但也要向前修复。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: It's not roll back a PR because it wasn't the thing we wanted to do.
zh: 并不是因为那不是我们想做的事就回滚一个 PR。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: It is, okay, cool, what we missed on the verification side that allowed this to land, either in a verifier if it's a human concept, or on tests if it's something bad, so that we can continually fix forward and build those guardrails, earn that trust on the autonomy side that you mentioned.
zh: 而是，好吧，酷，我们在验证端漏掉了什么才让这个合并的，如果是一个人类概念的话就是在验证器中，或者如果是什么坏东西的话就是在测试中，这样我们就能持续向前修复并建立那些护栏，赢得你提到的自主端那边的信任。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: In terms of some of the more spectacular failure modes, um as part of this, we changed our core queue a lot uh in the early days because we weren't verifying it strongly enough.
zh: 关于一些更壮观的失败模式，呃作为这的一部分，我们在早期大量更改了我们的核心队列，因为我们没有足够强地验证它。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: And by what I mean by that is we would have a fix, actually, concretely, we had an issue where uh PR comments were being double counted.
zh: 我的意思是我们会做一个修复，实际上，具体来说，我们遇到了一个问题，呃 PR 评论被重复计算了。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: And so they would end up on the queue twice, and so you would get a agent in two different sandboxes responding to the queue.
zh: 所以它们最后会出现在队列里两次，所以你会得到一个智能体在两个不同的沙箱里响应队列。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: You could have race conditions where it might produce two different uh code uh commits as part of that.
zh: 你可能会有竞态条件，它可能会产生两个不同的呃代码呃提交作为那的一部分。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Sometimes the second sandbox would start up after the first one I already committed, so it would recognize, hey, the work's being done, but we just it wasn't very effective.

en: And the queue here, just for context of what the queue is, the queue is the list of tasks that the orchestrator needs to pull to then pass to an agent or do something with or something.
zh: 这里的队列，只是为了提供一下队列是什么的上下文，队列是编排器需要拉取的任务列表，然后传递给智能体或者用其做点什么或者其他什么。

en: Exactly.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Exactly.
zh: 正是。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: And so we would fix that, it'd be good for a day, then it would regress, then we'd fix it again, then it would regress, then we'd fix it again.
zh: 所以我们会修复它，它会好一天，然后它会退化，然后我们再次修复，然后它会退化，然后我们再次修复。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: There was a point where I think we had like 60 PRs over two or three weeks, or sorry, two or three days that were all trying to fix this.
zh: 有个时候我想我们大概在两三周内，或者对不起，两三天内有 60 个 PR，都试图修复这个。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Um and so this was just causing constant churn and frustration because we'd say we fixed it and then it would regress, and it was just it was a pain.
zh: 呃所以这只是造成了不断的动荡和挫败感，因为我们会说我们修好了，然后它会退化，这只是很痛苦。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: And so the way that we wanted to try to fix that because we were still going to continue to let agents do whatever they wanted, was really lean into the verification side on that.
zh: 所以我们想要尝试修复那个的方式是因为我们仍然要继续让智能体做任何它们想做的事，就是真正深入那一侧的验证。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: And so what we ended up doing was building a quint formal uh model of our Q behavior, um, specifically the uh independency of um being able to kind of add stuff to the queue so that we could uh verify that on every single PR that we hadn't broken that uh formal model.
zh: 所以我们最终做的是构建了一个 quint formal uh 模型来模拟我们的 Q 行为，呃，具体是那个 uh independency of um 能够把东西加到队列里，这样我们就能呃验证我们在每一个 PR 上都没有破坏那个 uh 形式化模型。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Um that took I wouldn't have known how to do that in pre-agent world, just flat out.
zh: 呃那花了我在前智能体世界里不会知道怎么去做那个，坦白说。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: I knew what a formal verification was, wouldn't have known how to actually build it.
zh: 我知道什么是形式化验证，但不会知道如何实际构建它。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Uh took me about a day with Fable and then using the Dark Factory to go implement this, and we've had absolutely zero reoccurrences of that after the fact.
zh: 呃花了大概我和 Fable 一天时间，然后使用 Dark Factory 去实施这个，从那以后我们绝对零次复发。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: And so that for us was very painful in the moment, particularly as we were scaling up.
zh: 所以这对我们来说在那一刻非常痛苦，特别是当我们正在扩大规模时。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Um, but then B, a really important insight of like, no, it's not just the kind of verification that we used before of like test and shared human context and like trust that a human has enough context about everything else going on to know that this is a sensitive part of the code base.
zh: 呃，但然后 B，一个真正重要的洞察，比如，不，这不仅仅是我们要以前用的那种验证，比如测试和共享的人类上下文，以及相信人类对所有其他正在进行的事情有足够的上下文来知道这是代码库的敏感部分。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: No, we actually have to lean in even firmer than we had before because agents don't have that contextual information and we don't want to give it to them because that burns to tokens, which is therefore more expensive and slower.
zh: 不，我们实际上必须比以前更深入地投入，因为智能体没有那个上下文信息，而且我们不想给它们因为那会烧掉 token，因此更贵也更慢。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Um so that was kind of one really interesting, annoying, frustrating bit of time.
zh: 呃所以那是一个真正有趣的、恼人的、令人沮丧的一段时间。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Um, the other one was an experiment we ran during the offsite, um, which I was really excited for and which really did not work the way I wanted it to, unfortunately.
zh: 呃，另一个是我们在这个外地期间运行的一个实验，呃，我对此非常兴奋，但遗憾的是真的没有按我希望的方式工作。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Um, and that was uh explicitly about stress testing this verification layer.
zh: 呃，那就是 uh 明确地关于压力测试这个验证层。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: My personal belief is that if we get our verification layer strong enough and if we are oriented around specifically the behaviors that we care about as an organization, not the actual implementation of the code, I don't care about if you how when I click a button on the UI, the results appear.
zh: 我个人的信念是，如果我们让我们的验证层足够强，并且我们是围绕作为一个组织我们关心的具体行为定向的，而不是代码的实际实现，我不在乎如果你当我点击 UI 上的一个按钮时，结果出现了。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: I care about when I click a button on the UI, the results appear.
zh: 我关心的是当我点击 UI 上的一个按钮时，结果出现了。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: And so we should be able to, just from that verification layer, be able to rebuild the entire system from scratch in a new language.
zh: 所以我们应该能够，仅从那个验证层，就能够从零开始在一种新语言中重建整个系统。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Um so we tried to do that.
zh: 嗯，所以我们尝试那样做。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Uh we currently are a Python implementation.

en: Uh Elixir is-ish a good fit for this in terms of having uh kind of the actor model.

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: And so we took our verification layer only, so none of our unit tests, nothing um other than kind of our end-to-end tests, our integration tests, this formal uh model that we were talking about, um, and some of the properties that we uh that we verify kind of on the surface boundary rather than on internal dynamics.
zh: 所以我们只拿出了我们的验证层，所以没有我们的任何单元测试，没有任何东西，除了某种我们的端到端测试、我们的集成测试、我们谈论的那个形式化模型，以及我们验证的一些属性，这些是在表面边界上而不是在内部动态上的。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: And we gave that to a coding agent to then go plan out and uh building that in Elixir from scratch.
zh: 然后我们把它给了一个智能体，去规划并在 Elixir 中从零开始构建它。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Um and then we went into that.
zh: 呃然后我们深入研究了那个。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Um that worked, it built something, but we hit kind of two major roadblocks that kind of prevented us from being able to call this a success.
zh: 呃那行得通，它构建了一些东西，但我们遇到了两个主要障碍，阻碍了我们能够称之为成功。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: One thing I will note, our Q was perfect.
zh: 我想指出的一件事是，我们的 Q 是完美的。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Q worked totally fine.
zh: Q 运行得完全正常。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: So the formal model held up well there.
zh: 所以形式化模型在那里经受住了考验。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: But what it ended up identifying was even after kind of all the investments on verification we thought we had made, we had some pretty big blind spots.
zh: 但它最终指出的是，即使在我们认为我们在验证方面进行了所有投资之后，我们仍然有一些相当大的盲点。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: We weren't actually verifying formally anything to do with the labels on linear, which are a very important routing mechanism.

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: That was all just built into unit tests, and our end to end tests were just testing the happy path there.

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: And so uh when we ported over the end-to-end test, oh shoot, suddenly our um suddenly the way that we were stacking PR is broke because that wasn't tested in an end-to-end test.
zh: 所以当我们迁移端到端测试时，哦糟糕，突然我们……突然我们堆叠 PR 的方式坏了，因为这没有在端到端测试中测试过。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: That was just in uh unit test.
zh: 那只是在……单元测试中。

en: So that's core functionality that wasn't verified externally and so was broken in the Elixir implementation.
zh: 所以那是没有在外部验证的核心功能，所以在 Elixir 实现中坏了。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: We weren't able to kind of push out to production, um, even though we run in a sandbox production environment.

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: And so then I had to manually babysit an agent to go do that.
zh: 所以我必须手动看护一个智能体去做那件事。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: And so that's an area where we want to be investing in in terms of getting the dark factory to be able to make non-destructive changes in production environments, um, or at least the sandbox environment first and then eventually production environments to take the human out of the loop there.

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Um and then finally, there was just some other bits of the functionality.
zh: 呃最后，还有一些其他功能部分。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: I mentioned the stacking of PRs um in terms of a feature branch, I mentioned the labels, um, I mentioned, or rather, there's also uh some of our GitHub functionality, specifically in terms of not just comments, but on CI batching where we try to take in all of the signals on CI failures and send them as a single as a one-off rather than uh sending them as a sequence that isn't captured by an N10 test.
zh: 我提到了在 feature branch 方面堆叠 PR，我提到了标签，嗯，我提到了，或者说，还有我们的部分 GitHub 功能，特别是不仅在评论方面，而且在 CI batching 方面，我们试图接收 CI 失败上的所有信号，并将它们作为一个一次性发送，而不是作为一个未被 N10 测试捕获的序列发送。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: So there was some pretty core functionality and improvements to the system that weren't being captured by this verification layer.
zh: 所以有一些相当核心的功能和系统改进没有被这个验证层捕获。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: And so despite really wanting to turn it on, well, I did turn it on and then it immediately broke and then I fixed it, and then it turned on again, and then it broke some people's PRs, and I had to be like, okay, cool, this didn't work.
zh: 所以尽管非常想开启它，嗯，我确实开启了它然后它立刻坏了然后我修复了它，然后又开启了，然后它搞坏了一些人的 PR，我不得不想说，好吧，酷，这没起作用。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Um, and so I think the real learning from that is this I think is doable.
zh: 嗯，所以我认为真正的经验教训是，我认为这是可行的。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: We got pretty far with it.
zh: 我们在这方面走得相当远。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: I think it is an even more ambitious framing though than what Anthropic did with the Rust rewrite, where they had kind of the original Zig source code as an input to that.
zh: 我认为这是一个比 Anthropic 用 Rust 重写所做的更宏大的框架，在他们的案例中，他们拥有原始的 Zig 源代码作为输入。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: But I think it actually allows you to write idiomatic code better because our Elixir implementation, I'm not Elixir expert, so this is entirely LLM as a judge, agent vibed.

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Our Elixir implementation evidently was idiomatic elixir.
zh: 我们的 Elixir 实现显然是地道的 elixir。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: I don't really know how to assess that, but evidently so, uh, rather than being Python 2 Elixir ported.
zh: 我真的不知道如何评估那个，但显然是这样，而不是 Python 2 Elixir 移植的。

speaker: Rob Willoughby
en: Um, but we need to make sure that we cover everything.
zh: 呃，但我们需要确保我们要涵盖一切。
